kpis.name: S&P 500
kpis.note: Broad equity risk-on/risk-off signal. High VIX or S&P drawdown signals demand risk for Southwire construction end markets.

kpis.name: Brent Crude
kpis.note: Energy costs affect Southwire manufacturing and logistics. Sustained Brent >$90 pressures freight and resin input costs.

kpis.name: Copper (LME)
kpis.note: Primary raw material. Copper content of wire drives COGS. Sustained elevation compresses margin unless hedged or repriced.

kpis.name: Aluminum (LME)
kpis.note: Key input for aluminum wire and cable. Price signals secondary cost pressure and hedge calendar triggers.

kpis.name: Freight (Drewry WCI)
kpis.note: Ocean freight index drives import costs on raw materials and packaging. WCI >$4K signals elevated supply chain risk.
kpis.change: Monitor Drewry WCI weekly for rate momentum

kpis.name: VIX
kpis.note: Equity market fear gauge. VIX >25 indicates risk-off environment; monitor customer demand signals and receivables.

kpis.name: Natural Gas
kpis.note: Energy input for manufacturing and logistics. Sustained elevation pressures margin. Drives residential heating demand indirectly.

kpis.name: Gold
kpis.note: Risk sentiment indicator. Gold >$3,000 with VIX elevation signals macro uncertainty that may dampen CapEx spending by customers.

wire.title: Washington wildfires destroy homes, force thousands to evacuate
wire.summary: Spokane Mayor Lisa Brown says nearly half of the city's neighborhoods have either been evacuated or are at risk as the fires remain uncontained.

wire.title: U.S. men's national team coach Mauricio Pochettino will stay through 2030 World Cup
wire.summary: Pochettino came on in 2024 to right the ship ahead of this year's World Cup, in which he led the team to a record three wins and helped ignite enthusiasm in millions of fans before a round of 16 exit.

wire.title: Todd Blanche rescinds 'anti-weaponization fund'. And, Trump calls off striking Iran
wire.summary: Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche rescinds President Trump's anti-weaponization fund ahead of his confirmation hearing. And, the president calls off strikes on Iran over a potential deal.

wire.title: What would it take to get peptides on the shelf?
wire.summary: An FDA advisory panel recently voted to green-light some popular peptides. The decision brought enormous attention to the market for these products — and concerns about the unregulated supply.

wire.title: For those with criminal records, AI is breaking down barriers to employment
wire.summary: Tens of millions of Americans have criminal records that can be barriers to employment. An AI-powered app is helping those eligible to expunge their records at a pace not seen before.

wire.title: Rare photos of ex-Myanmar leader Aung San Suu Kyi give her family hope
wire.summary: Kim Aris, son of Aung San Suu Kyi, told NPR that photographs of his mother meeting a foreign official gave him "a reason to hope" for the first time since the military coup that ousted her in 2021.

wire.title: Over 4 million people are no longer receiving food aid amid sweeping changes to SNAP
wire.summary: SNAP, also known as food stamps, has seen a rapid and consistent participation decline since last July. The drop comes as the program faces historic cuts and changes.

wire.title: She protested ICE raids. Then agents showed up at her door
wire.summary: The Justice Department is using federal conspiracy charges to sweep up ICE protesters. Some legal experts worry the agency is casting too wide a net to prosecute political activists.

wire.title: Bedbugs, bad Wi-Fi: Federal workers say forced summer relocations have been chaos
wire.summary: Federal agencies are rushing to move hundreds of workers into new buildings. Employees say the moves are significantly disrupting their work.

wire.title: For Republicans planning post-Trump future, one race in Washington is worth watching
wire.summary: The primary to replace Rep. Dan Newhouse is a rare opportunity for Washington's Republicans to seek federal office. Candidates representing different wings of the party are testing Trump's influence.

wire.title: Russia says seven killed and 40 injured by Ukrainian drone hitting busy beach
wire.summary: Three children were killed when the drone crashed at a popular resort on the Black Sea.

wire.title: Rhine falls to record low levels as drought strains Europe's rivers
wire.summary: Low water levels in the Rhine, Danube and Po have curtailed the transport of goods and reduced electricity output.

wire.title: Iran says it is in talks with Oman but not the US after Trump says negotiations to resume
wire.summary: Iran's remarks that there were no talks with the US prompts Donald Trump to issue a strong condemnation of its leadership.

wire.title: Threat to oil tankers in Middle East  worst since start of Iran war, analysts say
wire.summary: Fresh attacks on alternative shipping routes have left tankers facing an increasingly complex situation, analysts say.

wire.title: 'My only son was shot standing up for justice' - inside city gripped by deadly protests in Pakistan-administered Kashmir
wire.summary: The BBC gains unique access to Rawalakot, scene of violent clashes between security forces and protesters in Pakistan-administered Kashmir.

wire.title: Russian anti-war politician says he has fled the country
wire.summary: Boris Nadezhdin, who was recently designated as a foreign agent, posted a video in front of the Eiffel Tower.
